messages:
Ava: morning — quick access q. I'm setting up a CI job that needs to toggle a feature flag in staging. Do I get a service account or do I use my user API key? (cc @mike)
Mike: congrats on week 1! For CI we prefer service accounts. Ping infra to create one with limited scopes.
Ava: thx — what's the name convention and which scopes?
Jenn: hey, use sa-ci-<team>-<env>.scopes: console.flags.write, console.read. We'll need a ticket to infra with env and retention.
Ava: can I self-serve via the console? I only see "Request access" button
Mike: no, service acc creation is infra-only. But you can create API tokens for yourself for short term if you need to test: Console > My tokens > Create -> choose "development" scope.
Ava: got it. Any runbook? would rather avoid perms mixups
Oscar: link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/sa_ci_onboarding — includes sample terraform snippet and least-priv YAML. Also add the service account to the FF owner group for the flag.
Ava: sample terraform snippet?
Oscar: 
```
resource "redwood_service_account" "ci" {
  name = "sa-ci-research-staging"
  scopes = ["console.flags.write","console.flags.read"]
}
```
Mike: when you open the infra ticket, include: repo, pipeline id, env, and the flag names. infra will whitelist IPs if needed.
access-bot: Your access ticket #3457 created by Ava. Status: awaiting infra review :hourglass: 
Ava: thanks all — filing ticket now. cc @jenn if we need extra scope for flag rollouts
Jenn: happy to help with rollout policy once infra returns the SA. :thumbsup:
